hosting_provider: Self-hosted Docker (bkimminich/juice-shop) on Kali lab VM
tech_stack: Node.js 24.22.2, Express, Angular SPA, Juice Shop 20.4.0-SNAPSHOT
risk_note: HIGH - listens on every interface (reachable from the whole LAN), ACAO: * with PUT/PATCH/DELETE allowed cross-origin, no CSP/HSTS, plain HTTP only.

CRITICAL - open listing hidden only by robots.txt; serves a KeePass DB, .bak source/dependency files and confidential docs; /ftp/order_ returns 403 so an extension filter exists and is worth bypass testing.
HIGH - second open listing (9.6 KB) of 'quarantined' files; anything parked here is downloadable by anyone.
CRITICAL - unauthenticated listing of key material; if a JWT signing key is here, every session token can be forged.
HIGH - server access logs downloadable without auth; logs typically carry IPs, URLs with tokens and other users' activity.
MEDIUM - 26 KB of unauthenticated internals: exact Node v24.22.2, memory, request counts per route; free fingerprinting and route discovery.
HIGH - 36 KB full app config served to anonymous users under an /admin path; shows broken access control and leaks feature flags/settings.
LOW - discloses exact build 20.4.0-SNAPSHOT, which lets an attacker match known CVEs; small on its own.
MEDIUM - public API documentation (301 to Swagger UI) hands an attacker the B2B API schema and parameters.
HIGH - machine-to-machine order API that accepts complex structured input; prime target for injection / server-side code-evaluation and resource-exhaustion testing once a token is obtained.
HIGH - main credential entry point; test for SQL injection in email field, brute force / missing lockout and user enumeration via error messages.

auth_type: Bearer JWT for GET (401); POST registration open
risk_note: HIGH - registration is anonymous; test mass assignment (e.g. setting a role field) and whether the list is readable with any low-privileged token.
MEDIUM - echoes identity from the token; useful oracle for testing forged/tampered JWTs and any reflected fields.
HIGH - account takeover path: reset relies on a security-question answer, and the question for any email is retrievable anonymously.
LOW - public list of questions; only matters because it feeds the password-reset attack above.
MEDIUM - second-factor logic; check verify for brute-forceable codes and whether disable needs re-authentication.
MEDIUM - newer auth mechanism (500 on bare GET = unhandled input); fresh code is often less hardened.
HIGH - anonymous query parameter fed into a product lookup (27 KB returned for empty q); top candidate for SQL injection and reflected XSS via /#/search.
MEDIUM - full catalogue readable anonymously; CORS pre-flight allows PUT/DELETE so test whether writes are enforced server-side.
MEDIUM - user-submitted comments returned to everyone; stored-XSS sink and leaks user IDs; check if POST lets you set someone else's UserId.
MEDIUM - 6 KB of user photo-wall posts with user data readable anonymously; also an upload sink.
LOW - 69 KB + 99 KB training metadata; in a real app this would be internal data exposure, here it is a map of where the bugs are.
HIGH - numeric basket IDs in the path; classic IDOR test (read/modify another user's basket with your own token).
HIGH - stores addresses and payment cards (PII/PCI); IDOR or over-broad GET here exposes the most sensitive data in the app.
MEDIUM - money and paid-tier logic; test negative amounts, race conditions and buying membership without paying.
MEDIUM - anonymous lookup by order ID (500 when the ID is missing = unvalidated input); test NoSQL injection and order-ID enumeration.
MEDIUM - order data for users and the accounting role; check horizontal/vertical access control.
HIGH - file upload; test type/size checks, XML upload (XXE), zip handling and where files land (/assets/public/images/uploads).
MEDIUM - public folder where user uploads are served back; if file type is not enforced, uploaded HTML/SVG becomes stored XSS on the app's own origin.
HIGH - server-side rendered page that takes user input (username, image URL); test SSTI on username and SSRF via image-from-URL.
MEDIUM - allow-listed redirect seen in JS (to=http...); test allow-list bypass for open redirect / phishing.
MEDIUM - server-rendered GDPR form that errors (500) on bare GET; test hidden parameters for local file inclusion.
MEDIUM - stores client IP for display later; if it trusts headers like X-Forwarded-For/True-Client-IP it is a stored-XSS sink.
MEDIUM - free-text input to a server-side bot; test logic abuse (coupon extraction) and injection into bot training data.
LOW - anonymous real-time channel for notifications; check that events cannot be spoofed by clients. Bare /socket.io GET is just the SPA shell.

tech_stack: Express server-rendered page + MP4 (2.2 MB) with subtitles
risk_note: LOW - static promo page; only interesting if subtitle content is injectable (XSS). /Video is the same file (case-insensitive routing).
MEDIUM - anti-automation on feedback; captcha is a JSON maths expression, so check whether it is solvable by script or reusable.
LOW - training-progress codes; no user data, only relevant to the score-board.

auth_type: Role check in Angular + JWT on backing APIs
risk_note: MEDIUM - admin UI route visible in the JS bundle; the client-side role check is bypassable, so real protection depends on /api/Users etc. enforcing roles.
LOW - hidden routes disclosed by headers and security.txt; useful recon breadcrumbs, no server-side data of their own.
LOW - blockchain features call out to external chains; contract logic is out of scope for a web test, note only.
LOW - intended public metadata; value is only that robots.txt points straight at /ftp and security.txt at /#/score-board.
LOW as assets (not real endpoints: prefix catch-alls), but every unknown path returns a verbose Express error page ('Error: Unexpected path') - framework disclosure.
NOT WORTH LOOKING via GET - returns the same 9,984-byte SPA shell as any unknown path, so it is not a distinct server resource.
OUT OF SCOPE - Docker's container runtime on the lab host, bound to loopback only; not part of Juice Shop, excluded from testing.
